description:
One production image serves the built web UI and Rust API from a single correctly supervised non-root jit-server process against a mounted repository.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The multi-stage build completes web/dist before compiling jit-server with usable embedded assets, and runtime smoke serves both the SPA root/fallback and /api/health.
- [hard] REQ-02: The runtime declares numeric non-root default 10001:10001, contains no nginx, Node, MCP server, or CLI service, and launches the signal-aware jit-server as PID 1 through an exec-form ENTRYPOINT or CMD.
- [hard] REQ-03: The runtime declares WORKDIR /repo and starts the server there, accepts an explicit numeric UID:GID override, requires /repo and /repo/.jit to be readable and writable by that effective identity, fails clearly otherwise, and never changes host ownership or permissions from inside the container.
- [hard] REQ-04: With either a repository prepared for 10001:10001 or a UID:GID mapped to the host repository owner, the image passes --data-dir /repo/.jit, starts read/write behavior without auto-initializing the repository, and preserves linked document access plus host-visible .jit changes.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each runtime fixture seeds distinguishable issue and linked-document terms inside the mounted repository, calls the web-used /api/search route, and proves both issue and document results come from /repo; a healthy server that searches the image build filesystem fails smoke.
- [hard] REQ-06: The image health check targets /api/health. Both runtime fixtures configure a ten-second Docker/Podman stop timeout, send SIGTERM with multiple SSE plus a deliberately stalled ordinary response/connection active, observe prompt SSE EOF, forced ordinary close at the application five-second deadline, connection-count/deadline logs, and exit 0 before ten seconds; SIGKILL/137 fails.

## Notes

Blast radius: root `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, focused image-runtime fixtures, and the server's embedded static-asset fallback. The user-authorized server change is limited to SPA routing and cache behavior; no domain, storage, or API behavior changes.

Legacy Compose definitions, split-image files, and active deployment scripts and documentation are a successor cutover performed only after this replacement image passes runtime smoke. This issue leaves those predecessor surfaces unchanged; its completed image contract unblocks their deletion and migration rather than asserting repository-wide topology convergence.
title: Build the single server and web production image
